agent left out.effect: Advection of sensible heat by vapor and air fluxes
Pressure work and changes in total pressure
agent left out.why: Total pressure in the pore is nearly constant on the time scales of sublimation. $\partial_t p$ is many orders of magnitude smaller than $C\,\partial_t T$.

agent left out.effect: Kinetic energy and viscous dissipation of the gas
agent left out.why: Gas speeds are tiny (mm/s or less), so $\rho u^2/2$ is negligible next to the enthalpies (about $10^6$ J/kg).
The expansion coefficient is about $10^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$, so the extra terms are of relative order $10^{-4}\,\Delta T$.

agent left out.effect: Interfacial (surface) energy and curvature (Gibbs-Thomson) correction to the latent heat
agent left out.why: $\gamma/(\rho_i L\,r) \approx 0.1/(920\cdot2.8\times10^6\cdot10^{-6}) \approx 4\times10^{-5}$ for curvature radius $r \approx 1\,\mu$m. The phase-field equation for $\phi$ is a later task.

Effective radiative conductivity $4\sigma T^3\ell \approx 4\cdot5.7\times10^{-8}\cdot8\times10^6\cdot10^{-4} \approx 2\times10^{-4}$ W/(m K), small next to the conductivity of ice (about 2-4 W/(m K)). It matters only in nearly empty, large pores.
These cross effects are second order in dilute vapor diffusion.

agent left out.effect: Heat exchange with the regolith grains
agent left out.why: The task restricts the domain to the pore space. The grains enter only through boundary conditions.
